items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: that’s how I’ve met my dream prince of all time, that I’ve never gotten over, Lawrence Brown. And he was my favorite. And so I sat next to him and we talked. I did a memorial for him

ctx.x: At that time, jazz was the popular music, isn’t that right?

Yes. You know my first job I was a society reporter in Chicago on first The Tabloid, which is now known as the Sun Times, and then the Hearst paper. And everybody in my age group was coming out. So there were debutante parties. And it was perfect for me, because they all had wonderful bands. The first time I ever heard Ray Nance was covering a debut of a girl named Bird Littlefield in Chicago. She had a coming out party at the Blackstone Hotel. And I think there was sort of a balcony around the ballroom and off…

at St. Peter’s Church here. And he died in California, but I thought I’d do it here, because I had a lot of stuff on him. I had slides and photographs and a lot of details. And I said at the memorial that he always looked like Rudolph Valentino to me. And I said if Rudolph Valentino could play the trombone, he’d probably sound like Lawrence.
